scenes.screen: Title card: scattered systems, then the Wabi Insight wordmark and tagline.
beats: Every organization runs on data. But the answers people need are locked inside different systems, and getting them usually means waiting days for a report.
Meet Wabi Insight, by WabiTex Solutions. Ask a question in plain English or Arabic, and get a verified answer from your own databases in seconds. Securely.

scenes.screen: Twelve industry tiles, SQL Server and Oracle chips, contact details of WabiTex Solutions.
beats: Wabi Insight is built for any organization: banks and insurers, airlines and airports, hospitals, government entities, retailers, telecom operators, universities, logistics companies, hotels, energy and manufacturing.
If your data lives in SQL Server or Oracle, Wabi Insight can work with it. Contact WabiTex Solutions for a demo on your own data, and we will organize the setup together with your team.

scenes.screen: Animated flow: question → AI plan → validation and permissions → read-only SQL → verified answer; output types.
beats: Here is how it works. Your administrators connect your databases with read-only accounts, and decide exactly which tables, columns and rows each role may see.
When someone asks a question, the AI writes a structured plan, never SQL. Wabi Insight checks that plan against the person's permissions, builds a safe, read-only query, and runs it on your database.
So every number on the screen comes from a verified query.

scenes.screen: Wabi Bank card: five systems and the eight sample people (fictional data).
beats: Let's see it working on Wabi Bank, a fictional bank with five systems: personnel, core banking, finance, digital banking and the IT help desk, and staff in many different roles.

scenes.screen: Clara Ashby (Organization Administrator, w1001): Organization Dashboard KPIs; Applications (stored connection test); Metadata (Customers object and its columns); Roles; Permissions (Branch Manager on CORE-BANKING); Organization Users and the New user form.
beats: Clara is the bank's organization administrator. Her dashboard shows users, sign-ins and activity, for her organization only.
Under Applications, she connects each system. Every connection is encrypted on the server, and tested to confirm it can only read.
The catalogue lists each table and column, with English and Arabic names, descriptions and a data classification. Only approved objects can ever be queried.
Roles describe what people do, and permissions are set per role. A branch manager, for example, reads core banking only for their own branch, and never sees restricted columns.
Users are added with their department, section and roles, and receive their temporary password by email.

scenes.screen: Victor Lindley (Management, w1002) on Ask Wabi Insight: picks CORE-BANKING, suggested questions, asks for deposit balances by branch; answer with chart, figures and narrative; 'How this was computed' expanded.
beats: Now Victor, the chief executive. On the Ask page he chooses a system, and types his question, or picks one of the suggested ones.
In seconds: a chart, the verified figures, and a written explanation of what they mean.
How this was computed explains, in plain words, which data was used and how it was grouped and filtered. And every query is logged on the server for accuracy reviews.

scenes.screen: Victor asks IT-HELPDESK for a dashboard of 2025 incidents: KPI cards and several charts.
beats: Ask for a dashboard, and Wabi Insight builds one: headline numbers, trends and breakdowns, each from its own verified query.
Here are all the IT incidents of the year, by priority, by month and by support group.

scenes.screen: Victor asks CORE-BANKING for a study of 2025 cheque returns; the PDF report card; pages of the generated PDF.
beats: For deeper questions, ask for a study. Wabi Insight runs up to ten queries, explains what stands out, and writes a complete PDF report.
The report has a cover, contents, charts, findings and recommendations, ready to download and share.
Every figure in it is the same verified data you saw on screen.

scenes.screen: Victor asks for an email draft (no attachment), then a FINANCE report with an email to the finance committee (PDF attached); copies the draft.
beats: It also writes your emails. Ask for an email, and you get a ready-to-send draft built on the verified figures.
Ask for a report and an email together, and the PDF report is attached to the draft. Here, Victor asks for third-quarter expenses against the revised budget, for the finance committee.
The report is attached, the email is written, and one click copies it.

scenes.screen: Language switched to Arabic (right to left); an Arabic question on PERSONNEL and its Arabic answer.
beats: And everything works in Arabic too: right to left, with Arabic numbers and dates.

scenes.screen: My History list; a saved analysis re-run (new version kept beside the old one); favorite, Word and Excel exports, a new collection.
beats: Every answer is saved in My History, with its question, its type and its cost.
Open one to see its versions. Run it again later, and you get a new version without losing the old one.
Mark favorites, group analyses into collections, and export to PDF, Word or Excel.

scenes.screen: The generated files: PDF study pages, the Word document and the Excel workbook.
beats: These are real files created by Wabi Insight: a PDF study, a Word document and an Excel workbook. My Reports keeps every one of them.

scenes.screen: Victor shares the study with Martin Calder (message, 30-day expiry); Martin's Shared With Me; the email dialog with the data-classification check.
beats: Share an analysis with a colleague, with a message and an expiry date. They see exactly what you saw. Nothing is queried again.
Or send it by email. Wabi Insight checks the data's classification first: restricted data never leaves the organization, and confidential data needs your explicit approval.

scenes.screen: Daniel Hartwell (branch manager, Deira): tellers of his branch only; Emily Carver (teller): her own postings; Sophie Langley (HR officer): Emirates ID column withheld; Clara's Support Access page.
beats: Permissions apply to every single question. When the Deira branch manager asks for cash deposits per teller, only Deira's tellers come back, and the answer says so.
A teller asking about cash sees only her own postings.
And when the HR officer asks for Emirates ID numbers, that column is restricted for her role, so the AI never even sees it.
Each organization's data is fully separated, every action is audited, and even platform support can only come in with your approval.

scenes.screen: Victor's Monitoring Rules: describes a rule in plain words, reviews the AI draft, saves it.
beats: Wabi Insight also works for you when nobody is asking. Monitoring Rules watch your data on a schedule.
Describe a rule in plain words. Wabi Insight drafts it, and you review it before saving.
Each rule runs under its owner's permissions, never more.

scenes.screen: Laura Bexley (Compliance, w1007): alert list and bell; cash-deposit alert detail; note and acknowledge; KYC access alert; daily digest preview.
beats: When a rule fires, an alert appears, and the right people are notified.
Here, an individual customer deposited just under fifty thousand dirhams in cash on several days, then fifty-eight thousand in a single day.
Laura acknowledges it with a note. Alerts inform people; they never block anyone automatically.
Access rules watch how data is used, too. When someone outside compliance looks up KYC documents, compliance is alerted. And everyone can get one daily digest.

scenes.screen: Victor creates a weekly periodic report (PDF) of the cheque study for two recipients and runs it now.
beats: Need the same report every week? Periodic Reports email a saved analysis on a schedule, as PDF or Excel.
Each recipient receives figures computed under their own permissions.

scenes.screen: Clara: Organization Insights metric; Support Desk new request form.
beats: Administrators also see how Wabi Insight is used in their organization: users, sign-ins and activity, over any period.
And the Support Desk tracks every request with the WabiTex team, from first message to resolution.
